methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $15M total raised proxy.

private.name: Cobod
private.rationale: Same sector (Housing & Construction), same stage (Series A)

data.narrative:
Material Evolution, a Series A stage housing and construction company founded by Liz Gilligan and Sam Clark, has raised $15M to date. The valuation analysis is constrained by a limited comparable universe: one identified private peer (Cobod) and no public comparables in the frontier construction technology space. This scarcity limits triangulation depth and increases reliance on stage-based methodology.

Stage-progression analysis, the sole applicable method given data availability, uses the $15M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-stage progression. This yields an implied valuation of $30M. The method assumes that capital deployed to date reflects reasonable early-stage value creation and that typical step-up multiples hold for this sector positioning.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, with a median point of $30M. Key uncertainties stem from the sparse comp set—the single private peer provides limited benchmarking—and structural questions about whether standard stage-progression multiples apply to frontier construction technology, where market adoption and regulatory pathways remain nascent. Revenue traction, capital efficiency relative to Cobod, and pathway to Series B fundraising visibility would meaningfully narrow this range.
